title: Hybrid traffic + synthetic eval orchestrator for staged AB/config flips
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Recent config and model flips have produced subtle quality regressions that only appear in specific user cohorts or long-tail prompts. Existing canary checks rely either on synthetic probing or traffic sampling alone; both have gaps. Synthetic probes can miss real-world distribution drift and user-reported regressions, while blind traffic sampling lacks signal for low-volume cohorts and rare failure modes.

Objective: Build a hybrid evaluation orchestrator that combines: (1) mirrored production traffic for golden-cohort shadowing, (2) targeted synthetic probe suites, and (3) small A/B exposures for probabilistic validation — all tied into an automated rollback policy controlled by statistically principled sequential tests. The orchestrator should minimize false positives while catching high-risk regressions early and enabling automatic safe rollback when warranted.

Scope: MVP covers config flips and minor model variant swaps for hosted and dedicated deployments. Private deployments will be supported in a follow-up iteration (API surface kept compatible). The system will integrate with existing eval metrics, Redwood Console dashboards, and the rollback actuator service.

Design highlights:
- Golden cohort mirroring: mirror a subset of traffic (10–20% of requests from high-value routes) to the candidate variant in shadow mode. Responses are recorded and compared offline against baseline using multi-metric diffs (semantic-similarity, toxicity score delta, response latency, and token-efficiency).
- Targeted synthetic probes: run a curated set of 2k prompts per rollout that exercise known edge behavior and regression-prone patterns. Probes run continuously and are weighted higher for early-stage validation.
- Adaptive A/B micro-exposure: expose a small fraction (0.5–2%) of live traffic as real A/B traffic with attribution/consent where required. Use staggered ramping: 0.5% -> 1% -> 2% over configurable windows with manual gating optional.
- Statistical engine: use Bayesian sequential hypothesis testing (Beta-Bernoulli for binary metrics, Gaussian sequential tests for continuous) with configurable priors and false discovery rate control across multiple metrics. Support hysteresis to avoid flip-flopping.
- Rollback policy: automatic rollback triggers when posterior probability of degradation > 97.5% on any high-priority metric or when a composite score (weighted metrics) exceeds threshold for N consecutive windows. Rollbacks are orchestrated through the rollout controller with tagged audit events and auto-created incident tickets.
- Explainability & provenance: every evaluation run stores the prompt set, model/config hash, kernel/quantization profile, sampling seeds, and snapshot of KV-cache heuristics. Console shows diff visualizations and the top contributing inputs.
- Cost controls: dynamic throttling of shadow traffic and probes to keep incremental inference cost under a configurable budget per rollout.

Operational playbook:
- Preflight: run full synthetic probe set in CI gated by eval pass/fail.
- Stage 1: mirror golden cohort + synthetic probes for 24h. Manual review required if any high-priority metric trends up.
- Stage 2: A/B micro-exposure with sequential testing windows. If tests pass, escalate to broader staged rollout. If tests fail, automatic rollback and post-mortem.

Non-goals: handling of large architecture swaps (major model family changes) and full private deployment air-gapped evaluation in v1.
acceptance_criteria: Orchestrator can create and run a hybrid evaluation pipeline for a given rollout within the console
Bayesian sequential test implementation returns stable posterior estimates for binary and continuous metrics and exposes decision thresholds
Automatic rollback executes within 60s of decision trigger and records an audit event with evidence (metric diffs + top failing inputs)
Cost throttles ensure incremental inference spend for shadow+probes does not exceed configured budget in 90% of pilot rollouts
End-to-end integration tests in CI that simulate a synthetic regression and confirm rollback is triggered
tasks: Design API contract for evaluation pipelines (JSON schema for probe sets, mirror routes, metric weights)
Implement mirror proxy hooks to duplicate traffic and annotate trace IDs for comparison
Ship Bayesian sequential-test library and integrate it with the metrics ingestion pipeline
Dashboard UI: rollout status, metric posterior curves, top contributing prompts, and rollback button
Implement rollback actuator endpoint and tie into rollout controller for automatic reversion
Create curated synthetic probe corpus and tagging for edge categories
End-to-end tests and chaos tests simulating partial telemetry loss
Run a pilot with 3 internal services (chat, summarization, code-generation) and collect feedback

risks: Shadowing high-volume routes may double inference cost if not throttled — mitigated by adaptive budget control
False positives from overly sensitive statistical thresholds may cause unnecessary rollbacks — mitigated by hysteresis and composite scoring
Data privacy concerns when mirroring user input — mitigation: automatic scrubbers and routing opt-out for PII-marked endpoints
Telemetry lag could delay decisions and allow regressions to reach more users — mitigation: prioritize low-latency metrics and sliding-window alarms
decisions: Use Bayesian sequential tests as primary decision engine for flexible early stopping
Require both synthetic AND mirror signals for auto-rollback on non-critical metrics; allow single-signal rollback for high-severity regressions
Expose configurable thresholds per project and per-metric with sane defaults managed by the SRE team
Pilot budgets default to $200 incremental inference spend per rollout unless overridden
